turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. [Name]. Yeah, um... well, I guess what really made me come in today is... well, it's work stuff, mostly. I work as a wholesale buyer, right? I got the job straight out of high school, worked my way up, and I'm only 22, so I know I have a lot to prove, but I'm good at what I do. I know my margins, I know my inventory. 

But lately... well, actually for a while now, I just can't shake the feeling that people at work are coordinating against me. And not just the people in the office, but even some of our outside vendors. I know they're tracking my buys. Like, they're monitoring everything I put into the system, every single purchase order, and they're deliberately messing with the launch numbers. It's like they're altering the data behind the scenes just to make me look completely stupid in front of the higher-ups. I mean, I'll set up a whole seasonal launch, perfectly calculated, and suddenly the projections and the final numbers are completely tanked, and it makes no sense at all unless someone is actively tampering with it. 

I actually took all this to my supervisor. I sat him down, I laid it all out for him, but he just... he pulled up the master reports and sat there trying to convince me that the numbers don't prove anything. He spent, like, forty-five minutes showing me all these spreadsheets saying, "Look, everything matches, nobody is messing with your buys, you're doing fine." But I know what I'm seeing. I know they're communicating behind my back to sabotage my launches, even if the reports look normal to him. They're just covering their tracks. It's just exhausting, honestly, having to watch my back every single second of the day, and trying to explain it to people who won't see it... so that's why I'm here.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that coworkers and vendors are conspiring to sabotage their work and alter data, maintaining this conviction even when presented with contradictory evidence by their supervisor.

turns.doctor_question: When you're at work or even outside of work, have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or comment on?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, um, actually... yeah, I have. It's, well, it's really unsettling, to be honest. It's not all the time, but it happens enough that I've started dreading certain parts of my day. Like, for instance, when I'm back in the stockroom—which I have to be a lot, obviously, because I need to physically check the inventory that comes in against my purchase orders, especially since I know they're messing with the numbers. I have to see the actual boxes with my own eyes. So I'll be back there, and it's usually pretty quiet, maybe just the hum of the HVAC or whatever, and I'll be counting units, and clear as day, I'll hear this man's voice. 

It sounds like he's standing right behind my left shoulder. Just right there. And he'll say something like, "Move faster, Scott," in this really demanding, almost mocking tone. Or, if I'm looking at a pallet of new seasonal stuff, I'll hear him laughing. Just this low, cruel laugh, like he knows the launch is going to tank because they've already rigged it. And I'll spin around, my heart just hammering in my chest, completely ready to confront whoever is sneaking up on me, but... the aisle is completely empty. There's nobody there. 

And it's not just at work, either. The other day, I was driving back from a vendor meeting across town. I was the only person in the car, windows rolled up, radio wasn't even on because I was trying to run the margin calculations in my head. And suddenly, from the backseat, I hear that same laugh. I almost swerved into the next lane. I checked the rearview mirror, I even pulled over at a gas station to check the back, but of course, it was empty. It's just... it's like someone is following me, constantly judging what I'm doing, but I can't ever catch them. I don't know how they're doing it, if it's some kind of directional speaker or what, but it's really starting to get to me. I mean, how are you supposed to focus on a multi-thousand dollar buy when someone is literally whispering in your ear and then vanishing?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses fixed, paranoid beliefs that others are 'messing with the numbers' and have 'rigged' the product launch.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly describes hearing a man's voice speaking to him and laughing when no one else is present, both in the stockroom and alone in his car.

turns.doctor_question: When you hear that voice or think about what's happening at work with the data being altered, do you ever have any doubt that it might not be real, or do you feel completely certain that it's actually happening?
turns.patient_response:
I mean, why would I doubt it? It's happening to me. I know it sounds crazy to other people, and I know my supervisor thinks I'm just stressed or misreading the spreadsheets, but I know what I'm seeing. I've been doing this job since I graduated high school. I know the inventory systems inside and out. I know the margins, I know the projections, and I know exactly what I put into the system for every single launch. 

So when I see the final numbers completely tanked, and the data in the system doesn't match what I know I entered, what else am I supposed to think? It's not a mistake. It's too calculated. It's like they're going in and altering the data behind the scenes just to make me look completely stupid in front of the higher-ups. And it's not just a one-time thing, either. It's happening over and over again, with different vendors, different product lines. I'll set up a seasonal launch, perfectly calculated, everything double-checked, and then bam, the numbers are completely off. 

And my supervisor, he just doesn't get it. I sat him down, I showed him everything, and he just pulled up the master reports and spent forty-five minutes trying to convince me that everything matches and nobody is messing with my buys. But of course the master reports look fine to him! If they're going through all the trouble to sabotage my launches, they're obviously going to cover their tracks on the master reports so they don't get caught. I mean, it's just exhausting having to constantly watch my back and try to explain this to people who just refuse to see what's right in front of them. So no, I don't doubt it. I know they're tracking my buys and messing with the numbers. I just don't know how to stop them.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses absolute certainty that coworkers are sabotaging their work and altering data, maintaining this fixed belief even when presented with contradictory evidence by their supervisor.

turns.doctor_question: If I told you that I checked with your supervisor and your vendor contacts, and they all said there's no actual evidence of anyone tampering with your data or tracking your purchases, would that change your mind about what's happening, or would you still believe they're coordinating against you?
turns.patient_response:
Honestly, doctor, that wouldn't change my mind even a little bit. I mean, if you really think about it, if you went to my vendor contacts or my supervisor and asked if they were tampering with my data, they are obviously going to deny it. They aren't just going to confess that they are altering the data behind the scenes. That is exactly what really made me come in today, because I just cannot shake the feeling that people at work and even some of our outside vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. 

I already went through this exact scenario with my supervisor, like I was telling you before. He sat me down and showed me all the master reports, going line by line, trying to prove that there is no evidence of anyone tampering with anything. He spent forever trying to convince me, but even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that anyone is messing with my stuff, it doesn't change what I know is happening. Seeing those spreadsheets didn't change my mind, so you asking them wouldn't either. I know what I entered into the system. I know my margins, I know the exact unit counts I ordered for these seasonal launches, and I double-check every single purchase order before it goes live. I have it all perfectly calculated on my end. 

So when the final numbers come back completely tanked and make me look like a total amateur to the higher-ups, I know it is because they are coordinating against me. It doesn't matter if the master reports look clean to my boss or if the vendors play dumb when you ask them. They are just covering their tracks. I mean, I am only 22, I got this job straight out of high school and worked my way up, so I know I have a target on my back. People are jealous, or they just want to see me fail and lose my position. So, no, hearing that they denied it wouldn't change my mind at all. It just proves how deep this whole thing goes and how good they are at hiding it from people who just blindly trust whatever the computer spits out.

turns.doctor_question: When you hear that voice in the stockroom or in your car, is there any part of you that wonders if it might be coming from inside your own mind, or do you feel absolutely certain it's an actual person or device tracking you?
turns.patient_response:
Inside my own mind? I mean... no, honestly, I don't see how that's even possible. Because you know the difference, right? Between thinking something and actually hearing a physical sound. Like, when I'm running margin calculations or projecting Q3 numbers, that's a thought. That's inside my head. I know what that feels like. 

But this... this is completely different. Like I was saying before, sometimes when I'm in the stockroom trying to verify the units, or like the other day driving back from a vendor meeting, I hear a man's voice, and it is entirely external. It's not a thought. It sounds exactly like it's coming from right behind me, like just inches away from my neck. When he says, "Move faster, Scott," or when he starts laughing at my picks for the seasonal launch—which is incredibly frustrating, by the way, because I put weeks of research into those picks—it has actual volume and pitch. In the stockroom, I can literally hear the sound of his voice bouncing off the metal shelving. You don't get room acoustics inside your own brain, you know? 

And that's exactly why I react the way I do. Because when I turn around—and I always turn around, completely expecting to see a guy standing right there in my personal space—nobody's there. It's just empty air. But if it was just in my mind, why would I have that physical reaction? Why would I whip around to look? I turn around because the sound waves are literally hitting my eardrums from the outside. I can hear the breath in his voice. So, no, I don't wonder if it's my mind playing tricks on me. It has to be some kind of directional audio tech, or maybe someone actually sneaking up on me and then ducking out of sight before I can catch them, because the voice is real. It's a real, physical sound happening in the room with me, and I just need to figure out how they're projecting it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient demonstrates a fixed belief that the voices are caused by 'directional audio tech' or someone sneaking up on him, despite the lack of evidence when he turns around.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly describes hearing a man's voice with actual volume and pitch coming from right behind him when no one is there, which is a clear auditory hallucination.

turns.doctor_question: Since this all started happening—the beliefs about people tampering with your data and hearing that voice—has there been any stretch of time, even a few days or a week, where you didn't feel like people were coordinating against you or you didn't hear that voice at all?
turns.patient_response:
A break? Like a stretch of time where it just stops? No. No, definitely not. I mean, I really wish there was, because that would be amazing to just have a weekend where I could actually relax and not have to log into the vendor portal from home on a Sunday night just to make sure nobody is messing with my pending orders. But if I really sit down and look at the timeline—and I have, because you have to document these things when you're dealing with this level of corporate sabotage—the suspicious stuff with my data and that guy's voice... they have been happening for roughly ten months now. 

Ten months of this, non-stop. Not a single week off. I know the exact timeframe because it all started right around when we were prepping for the spring transitional rollout. That's always a massive headache anyway, trying to forecast demand for transitional outerwear when the weather is unpredictable, dealing with overseas shipping delays, negotiating unit costs with the new vendors... and right in the middle of all that heavy lifting, that's when I first caught the margins being clipped in the system. And it was that exact same week when the voice first showed up right behind my neck in the stockroom while I was trying to do a physical count of the overstock. 

And ever since then, it has just been a constant, daily battle. Every single day, whether I'm on the floor, in the back office running the spreadsheets, or driving back from a meeting, I have to be on high alert. Ten months of constantly looking over my shoulder, ten months of keeping offline, hard-copy backups of my purchase orders in my briefcase just to prove to myself that I'm not the one making the mistakes when the final numbers come out wrong. So, no, there hasn't been a few days or a week where it stopped or where I didn't hear him laughing at me. If they actually took a week off from messing with me, I'd probably notice the spike in my quarterly performance immediately, but they don't let up. They just keep at it, day in and day out, for ten months straight.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses fixed, persecutory beliefs about 'corporate sabotage' and people 'messing with my pending orders' to clip their margins.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient clearly describes experiencing auditory hallucinations, specifically hearing a 'guy's voice' behind their neck and hearing him laughing at them.
symptom_reasoning.S079: The patient describes being in a persistent state of alertness, stating they are on 'high alert' and 'constantly looking over my shoulder' every single day.
